content: Can you give more detail: what do you find misleading?
Is it that the conclusion in the source is Continuous[induced f t, t] f, but rendered as Continuous f, i.e. omitting that continuity is w.r.t. two particular topologies?
why isn't docs#Topology.delabContinuous giving us something nice here?

Michael Rothgang said:

Can you give more detail: what do you find misleading?

Currently it reads: "Every function to a topological space is continuous."
While we are at it I think it would be great if topologies/measurable space structures were printed in the docs as they are in the code, although I guess it is not easy to do

I can imagine there are difficulties in automatically handling this in the doc. As a compromise, would it possible to have some form of doc annotation in the code that says "please print this implicit variable in the doc for this lemma"?

Martin Dvořák said:

Michael Rothgang said:

Can you give more detail: what do you find misleading?

Currently it reads: "Every function to a topological space is continuous."

Why not just add a docstring? It's clear from the statement that something funny is going on because alpha has no topology so the theorem as stated doesn't typecheck, so my reading of doc-gen is "there is missing information", which could be supplied in a docstring.

Martin Dvořák said:

I don't read docstrings.

Off-topic, but: ... why? I'm baffled. You do read Lean's error messages, right?

Aaron Liu said:

why isn't docs#Topology.delabContinuous giving us something nice here?

My guess is because it is scoped, so lean4#6050 applies here?

Michael Rothgang said:

You do read Lean's error messages, right?

Of course!
Anyways: I think we should both add a docstring and fix the underlying issue. If we only keep adding docstrings, we will probably overlook something.
